newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia IMF plan sees oil excise tax hike - C.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia IMF plan sees oil excise tax hike - C.Bank.

text.p: The Russian government has proposed raising the average duty paid by oil firms to 70,000 roubles per tonne of oil from 55,000 roubles as part of its fiscal programme with the International Monetary Fund, Central Bank First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksahenko said on Friday.
He said the proposal needed the approval of the State Duma lower house of parliament, but that support there was strong.
"The question of an oil excise tax increase must be settled through legislation," Aleksashenko told a news conference. "The question is now not under the government's control."
Aleksashenko said that an oil excise tax hike was originally proposed as part of the 1997 budget, but that it was dropped from the final budget when Duma deputies rejected it.
He said that a compromise was reached with oil companies not to increase excise duties in exchange for assurances that they would pay the existing rates in full.
"But it became clear that they were not paying 100 percent of the duties, and yet taxes had not been increased," he said.

Aleksashenko gave no further details of the proposed excise duty increase. The impact of any excise tax hike is likely to vary considerably among oil companies, which pay a wide range of duties under the current rates.

Under an deal reached early last year between Russia and the IMF, excise duties were hiked to 55,000 roubles per tonne from 39,400 roubles to compensate for a drop in oil export taxes, which the IMF said were not in line with free trade policy.
Oil pipeline tariffs were also increased last year to compensate for losses from the export duty reduction.
